en: Historical Fiction: A Case Study of Marie Antoinette
Historical Fiction: A Case Study of Marie Antoinette

body.value: The beginning of the shopping scene reveals Marie Antoinette's novelty and teenage instincts. A big close up shot and panning of a range of shoes. This emphasises that Maria Antoinette is in a position of luxury as well as the novelty of materialism.

This big close up shot of Marie Antoinette’s feet while trying on luxurious shoes with the Converse sneakers in the background emphasises that Maria is young and an inexperienced queen who takes pleasure in consumerism, revealing the human nature of teenage girls.
A wide shot of Marie and her ladies in waiting shopping and enthusiastically examining the range of colour fabrics indicates how social consumerism is being encouraged by her friends.
Medium close up low angle of a champaign tower which  displays the position of luxuries. The low angle gives a powerful stance.

Extreme close up shot of Marie trying on two different styles of necklaces. Historically necklaces are a symbol of status and wealth, but metaphorically represent consumerism as a centre of her life and how she views royalty.

Another close up shot of Marie trying on shoes and how the floor is untidy with champagne, food and cards on the floor to further emphasise the admiration of consumerism and teenage messiness and how Maria is still young.

Bird’s eye close up of fast cutting jump cuts of different luxury delicacies indicates the metaphor of being consumed by consumerism, as well as the juxtaposition of food in this scene being a symbol of luxury compared to survival.
High angle close up shot of Marie and her ladies in waiting relishing in gambling as a result of ignoring their court duties and ignoring the problem of the kingdom.

Close up shot of Marie with an extravagant hairstyle and indulging in luxury as a teenager would. The items of birds symbolise that Maria feels freedom from strict French court life when she engages in consumerism of luxury items. Marie directly looking at the audience reveals that she is only admiring herself and how luxury is the main focus of her life.

An extreme close up shot of one of Marie’s ladies in eating an extravagant dessert and this shot wants the audience to focus on this particular act and to have full attention of this shot. This shot also represents the indulgence of wealth.
A wide shot of Marie in her bedroom. The bedroom symbolises a place of comfort and refuge from the danger outside the Palace.
A medium shot of Marie being dressed in her robe by her maid emphasises the urgency to get to safety. The hand held camera gives a more personal and imitate feel to the scene.

A mid shot of Marie, one of her ladies and the maid quickly descending the stairs. This tracking shot embodies the audience to feel the urgency and danger of the situation. Marie is holding a candelabra captures Marie taking control over the situation to get her children and husband to safety.
A low angle wide shot of the French riot outside the Palace of Versailles. The symbolism of fire represents the rage of the French commoners against the King and Queen.

A low angle mid shot of Marie stepping out of the balcony and facing the riot. This powerful scene reveals Marie’s moment of bravery by putting herself at risk knowing people wish to kill her and her family. This scene represents a moment of accepting that the French people are against her and the monarchy. Importantly, Marie came out dressed in her robe which reveals that this particular act is not performative.

A mid shot of Marie bowing to the commoners. This powerful scene reveals that Marie is surrendering to the French people and unheard of that a Queen will bow to commoners. This shot is silent to place emphasis on the action.
